_reasons.er-npc-possess|VTABLE_WRITE|crates/er-np: NOT A GAME VTABLE. All three writes land inside a page THIS CRATE just obtained from `VirtualAlloc(NULL, ...)` -- `Thunk::build` reserves one page and fills it with a 55-slot vtable, 55 sixteen-byte forwarding stubs, and the 0x178-byte thunk object whose vptr and real-`ComManipulator` back-pointer those two `.write()` calls set. There is no module base, no RVA and no game address anywhere in the expressions; the class matches on the SHAPE of a function-pointer-table store, which is exactly what building a vtable looks like. Bounds are static and asserted on the host: `plan::TOTAL_BYTES` is computed from `OBJECT_BYTES + VTABLE_BYTES + SLOT_COUNT * STUB_STRIDE` and a test requires it to fit one 4 KiB page, a second test requires the three regions not to overlap, and a `const` assertion pins `OBJECT_BYTES == COM_SIZE + 8`. The ONE address in the page that the game ever sees is the object pointer written to `ChrCtrl+0x3b0` -- a heap field, reached by pointer chase from a reflection-resolved singleton, never by base+rva -- and `possess::teardown` clears it on every release path including DLL_PROCESS_DETACH, because `ChrCtrl::Unref` DLPanics on a non-null slot. Precedent: `er-quickload|VTABLE_WRITE|.../can_move_probe.rs` is granted for the same reason, that the store reaches a live object rather than a game image address.
_reasons.er-quickload|VTABLE_WRITE|crates/er-quic: IN BOUNDS, MEASURED 2026-09-01, and neither write reaches a game IMAGE address at all -- both store into a live HEAP object, which is why VTABLE_WRITE's `*(x as *mut T) = ..` shape matches them. Lines 130/131 write `this + 0x89c` / `this + 0x8a0` where `this` is the DETOUR'S OWN first argument, a pointer the engine passed in; there is no `base + rva` to gate. Lines 212/213 write the same two offsets on a device reached from `crate::game_rva(FD4_PAD_MANAGER_RVA)` -- the gate IS on that path -- and only after `*(device) == POLLED_DEVICE_VTABLE`, the vtable latched from the object the engine itself polled, so the class is confirmed at runtime rather than assumed. The object is `DLUID::PadDevice<DLKR::DLMultiThreadingPolicy>` (RTTI `.?AV?$PadDevice@VDLMultiThreadingPolicy@DLKR@@@DLUID@@`, vtable 0x1430c9f08 -> 0x1430cd048 with complete-object-locator offset 0, so `this` is the allocation base), which the DLUserInputManagerImpl device factory allocates as HeapAlloc(0xa68) = 2664 bytes in BOTH builds. The game's own poll (0x141f6bad0 -> 0x141f6d8d0, the only pointer to it in either image, at vtable+0x128) STORES both floats on this same `this`, so the offsets are in-bounds by construction. Frozen in scripts/check-object-field-offsets-1170.py: 4 field rows on the poll pairing (616/616 aligned, 72 offsets, zero moved), the FD4PadDevice 0x10/0x38 walk, the 0xa68 ALLOC_WITNESS and the PAD_STICK_LY WRITE_REACH bound.
